policy_title: Scrap Net Zero targets and related subsidies
stated: Reform UK will scrap Net Zero targets and associated subsidies, projecting savings of over £30 billion per year for the public sector. They will also scrap £10 billion of renewable energy subsidies through equivalent taxes.

source.quote: Scrap Net Zero and Related Subsidies Ditching Net Zero could save the public sector over £30 billion per year for the next 25 years. Scrap Annual £10 Billion of Renewable Energy Subsidies Achieve this through equivalent taxes on them.

bearing_set.reason: Scrapping Net Zero targets directly removes the UK's statutory emissions-reduction framework, materially affecting the emissions trajectory, climate pathway, and potentially air and water quality from continued fossil-fuel use.

Scrapping £10 billion of renewable energy subsidies (currently levied partly via energy bill charges) would have a direct and material — if contested — effect on household energy costs and real disposable income.

Removing £10 billion in renewable energy subsidies would reduce investment viability across the UK's offshore wind and solar sectors, directly affecting employment rate and job security for workers in those industries.

The policy's central fiscal claim — over £30bn/year in public-sector savings — is material enough to earn a real verdict on debt-path sustainability and whether spending is funded; whether the figure is credible is the contested judgment to be made.

Removing subsidy certainty for clean-energy investment materially affects UK green-sector business investment and long-run industrial competitiveness, while near-term energy-cost reductions for firms could improve productivity — a genuine dual-horizon prosperity effect distinct from the fiscal one.

membership_note: Four fundamentals earn real verdicts: O6 is the primary direct effect; O12 captures the large claimed fiscal saving; O2 is touched through the energy-bill levy mechanism; O13 reflects the contested investment and long-run competitiveness consequences.
